issues.suggestion: Blackstone appeared prominently yesterday in the Anthropic JV. Today it's a different story (data center REIT), but readers who saw yesterday's edition will notice the same name with another billion-dollar figure. issues.suggestion: Both editions lead nearly every item with a dollar figure as the hook. The effect is a parade of numbers that blur together. Vary the lead: start some items with what changed or what it means before revealing the price tag. E.g., lead with Palantir's 85% growth rate or Nscale's 66k GPUs deployment before the euro amount.

issues.previous_text: A Cerebras, fabricante de chips de IA de Sunnyvale, na Califórnia... A Anew Labs, unidade de descoberta de medicamentos da ByteDance (dona do TikTok)... A Linkerbot, startup de Pequim com dois anos de existência
issues.suggestion: The 'A [Company], [appositive clause describing what it does]' structure is used 4+ times in today's edition and was also frequent yesterday. It's good practice to explain companies (editorial principle #5), but varying the syntax avoids monotony. Try: 'A fabricante de chips programáveis Lattice Semiconductor vai...' or lead with the action: 'Para proteger identidades não-humanas, a Cisco comprou a israelense Astrix Security'.

summary: Moderate repetition: Trump-Xi summit countdown used as framing device in consecutive editions; Blackstone appears prominently two days in a row; internal 'Separadamente' doubled; dollar-figure-first leads and appositive company descriptions create structural monotony across both editions.
